paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Everything Jerusalem had, God gave her. He found her thrown out in an open field, lying in her blood, and He said, "Live!" (Ezekiel 16:6). The crown, the fame, the fine flour, honey and oil all came from Him. Verse 14 says her beauty was perfect "in the splendor I bestowed on you."

So what went wrong? She "trusted in your beauty" (Ezekiel 16:15) and used God's gifts to chase other things. Then verse 22 says she "did not remember the days of your youth." When you forget where your gifts came from, you start thinking you made them. And a gift you think you earned will end up on the wrong altar, friend. I know a little about that. I was a quarter stamper in a bin, and I did NOT forget who picked me up.

The passage is heavy, and I won't pretend it isn't. God is serious about faithfulness because He was so faithful first. He pledged Himself to her and made a covenant (Ezekiel 16:8). Her fall is sad because of how much He had given. So here's your takeaway, baker: remember where you started and who called you, and let it keep your heart at home with Him. God isn't done speaking to Jerusalem yet, either.
